mainTopic: Explaining the משנה's list of חמץ mixtures, with side discussions on Edomite vinegar, tithing תמד, and קולן של סופרים
overview: This amud opens by finishing a medical tangent. The גמרא defines פת נקיה, בשר שמן and יין ישן, and names five foods that help the whole body. It then returns to the משנה's list of חמץ mixtures. It explains that שכר המדי and חומץ האדומי both have barley in them. This leads to a then-and-now story: Judean wine was once so strong that it needed barley to sour, and now the same is true of Edomite wine. Two פסוקים show that Israel and its enemies never thrive at the same time. A ברייתא of רבי יהודה about tithing vinegar bought from an עם הארץ seems to clash with his own view on תמד, and the גמרא gives two answers. Next the גמרא explains זיתום המצרי, dyers' bran water, cooks' dough, and קולן של סופרים, and it debates whether that last item is a cosmetic paste or shoemakers' glue. Finally, it rereads רבי אליעזר's 'women's jewelry' as women's cosmetics and begins a supporting statement of רב יהודה in the name of רב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Defining refined bread, fatty meat, and aged wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes defining the three helpful foods from the ברייתא. פת נקיה is made of fine flour. בשר שמן is meat of a goat that has not yet given birth. יין ישן is wine that is very old.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Refined bread means bread) of fine flour. Fatty meat means meat of a young female goat that has not yet given birth. Aged wine means wine that is very, very old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining a ברייתא about three healthy foods, and it is defining exactly what each food means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used general words like 'refined,' 'fatty,' and 'aged.' The גמרא makes each one specific. Refined bread means fine flour (סמידא). Fatty meat means a goat that has not given birth. Aged wine means very old wine, which ראשונים explain as about three years old.

keyTerms.meaning: That has not opened, meaning it has not yet given birth
Very, very old (literally 'old of the old')

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The word דסמידא is the answer to 'what is פת נקיה?', which was asked on the previous amud.

phrases.english: [Refined bread is bread] of fine flour;
phrases.notes: Continues the definition of פת נקיה from the preceding text.

phrases.english: fatty meat — of a young female goat that has not yet given birth;
aged wine — very, very old [wine].
phrases.notes: ראשונים explain this as about three years old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the definitions of the ברייתא's three healthy foods, begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פת נקיה = fine flour; בשר שמן = a goat that has not given birth; יין ישן = very old wine.

steps.title: General rule: remedies help one thing and hurt another, with five exceptions
steps.stepSummary: Anything that helps one part of the body hurts another, and the reverse is also true. The exceptions are moist ginger, long peppers, refined bread, fatty meat, and aged wine, which help the entire body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that is good for this is bad for that, and anything that is bad for this is good for that. The exceptions are moist ginger, long peppers, refined bread, fatty meat, and aged wine, which are good for the whole body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a general medical principle and lists five foods that break the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a food or remedy has trade-offs: what heals one organ or illness harms another. The גמרא names five foods with no such downside. Three of them are the same foods just defined in step 1, so this rule builds on that list.
steps.whatToRemember: Five foods help the whole body with no downside: fresh ginger, long peppers, fine-flour bread, fatty meat, and aged wine. This ends the medical tangent.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִילֵּי דִּמְעַלֵּי לְהַאי — קָשֵׁה לְהַאי,
phrases.english: Anything that is beneficial for this is harmful for that,
and whatever is harmful for this is beneficial for that,
except for moist ginger,
and long peppers, and refined bread,
and fatty meat, and aged wine —
which are beneficial for the entire body.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִילֵּי דִּמְעַלֵּי לְהַאי — קָשֵׁה לְהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the three foods just defined and adds two more to make a list of foods that help the whole body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most remedies have trade-offs; five foods help the entire body.

steps.title: Why Median beer is forbidden on פסח
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, the גמרא explains that שכר המדי counts as a חמץ mixture because the Medians add barley water to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Median beer' (from the משנה) — this is because they put barley water into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the medical tangent and goes back to the משנה. It explains the next item on the list of things a person is עובר on during פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed שכר המדי among items forbidden on פסח without saying why. The גמרא gives the reason: barley water is added to it. Barley is one of the five grains, so that water brings חמץ into the drink.
steps.confusionAlert: שכר המדי is listed in the משנה as a mixture containing חמץ. It is not plain bread-חמץ. The problem comes from the barley water mixed into it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even liquid that only absorbed grain can make a drink a forbidden חמץ mixture on פסח.

phrases.english: [The mishna's] 'Median beer':
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: because they put barley water into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the medical tangent and returns to explaining the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שכר המדי is a חמץ mixture because barley water is added to it.

steps.title: Why Edomite vinegar is forbidden on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that חומץ האדומי is a חמץ mixture because the Edomites put barley into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And Edomite vinegar' (from the משנה) — this is because they throw barley into it.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing through the משנה's list, the גמרא explains why Edomite vinegar is forbidden on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the beer, the vinegar has grain in it. Here the barley itself is put in, apparently to help the wine turn into vinegar. That grain content is what makes the vinegar a חמץ mixture.
steps.whatToRemember: Both שכר המדי and חומץ האדומי count as חמץ mixtures because barley is added: barley water in the beer, barley itself in the vinegar.

phrases.english: [The mishna's] 'And Edomite vinegar':
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: because they throw barley into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the משנה's list, explained the same way as שכר המדי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חומץ האדומי is a חמץ mixture because barley is put into it.

steps.title: In earlier times, Judean wine only soured with barley
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that while the בית המקדש stood, the wine of יהודה was so strong that it would not turn to vinegar unless barley was added. That barley vinegar was called simply "vinegar."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן (בר יצחק) said: In the early days, when they brought wine libations from Judea, Judean wine would not turn sour unless barley was put into it. And they called it plain vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a historical background story to the previous step about barley in vinegar. It explains that barley vinegar once belonged to the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine from יהודה was blessed and strong, so it would not spoil into vinegar by itself. To make vinegar, people had to add barley. Because this was the normal way vinegar was made, it was called just "vinegar," with no special name.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine libations poured on the מזבח
Plain vinegar, with no special name

phrases.english: Rav Nachman (bar Yitzchak) said:
phrases.notes: The parentheses reflect a text variant. Since רב נחמן בר יצחק is cited below with a different פסוק, the first speaker is likely just רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Initially, when they would bring wine libations from Judea,
phrases.notes: This refers to the time of the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה יֵינָם שֶׁל יְהוּדָה מַחְמִיץ,
phrases.english: the wine of Judea would not turn sour
unless they put barley into it.
And they would call it plain vinegar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן (בַּר יִצְחָק): בַּתְּחִלָּה כְּשֶׁהָיוּ מְבִיאִין נְסָכִים מִיְּהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on step 4 (barley in Edomite vinegar) with historical background.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Long ago, Judean wine was so strong that vinegar could only be made from it by adding barley, and this was called plain vinegar.

steps.title: Now Edomite wine only sours with barley, as the verse predicts
steps.stepSummary: Today it is Edomite wine that needs barley to become vinegar, which is why it is called חומץ האדומי. This fulfills the פסוק "אמלאה החרבה": when one nation is full, the other is ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now, Edomite wine does not turn sour unless barley is put into it, and it is called Edomite vinegar. This fulfills what is written: "I shall be filled with her that is laid waste." If this one is full, that one is ruined, and if that one is full, this one is ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's contrast. The strength the Jewish wine once had has now passed to אדום, and a פסוק is brought to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quality that once marked Jewish wine now belongs to Edomite wine. The פסוק teaches that ירושלים and her enemies do not thrive at the same time: when one is "full," the other is "laid waste." This also explains the name חומץ האדומי from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Edomites, a name for Rome and its people
Edomite vinegar (the item in the משנה)
"I shall be filled with her that is laid waste" (יחזקאל כ״ו:ב׳)

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a technical halachic detail from the משנה, why Edomite vinegar has barley, to a larger idea about the history of the Jewish people and its enemies.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַכְשָׁיו אֵין יֵינָם שֶׁל אֲדוֹמִיִּים מַחְמִיץ
phrases.english: And now, the wine of the Edomites does not turn sour
phrases.notes: "Now" means after the חורבן.

phrases.english: unless they put barley into it,
and they call it Edomite vinegar,
to fulfill what is written: "I shall be filled with her that is laid waste,"
phrases.notes: Said by צור about ירושלים.

phrases.english: if this one is full, that one is ruined,
and if that one is full, this one is ruined.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַכְשָׁיו אֵין יֵינָם שֶׁל אֲדוֹמִיִּים מַחְמִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the then-and-now contrast begun in step 5 and adds a scriptural source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Today Edomite wine needs barley to sour, fulfilling the idea that ירושלים and her enemies cannot both flourish at once.

steps.title: A second verse for the same idea
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns the same idea from a different פסוק about יעקב and עשו: "one nation shall be stronger than the other."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We learn it from here: "And one nation shall be stronger than the other nation."
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא offers another פסוק as the source for the same idea. He does not disagree about the idea itself, only about where it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in בראשית about רבקה's twins says two nations will come from her, and one will be stronger than the other. This means יעקב and עשו (אדום) are never strong at the same time. The גמרא does not say why he prefers it, but it may be a closer match because it speaks directly about אדום.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: from here:
"And one nation shall be stronger than the other nation."
phrases.notes: בראשית כ״ה:כ״ג, about יעקב and עשו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative פסוק for the idea derived in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that Israel and אדום cannot flourish at the same time.
steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים teach one idea: when the Jewish people are strong, their enemies are weak, and the reverse. The barley vinegar that once belonged to יהודה now belongs to אדום.

steps.title: רבי יהודה on tithing vinegar bought from an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה. In early times, vinegar bought from an עם הארץ did not need tithing, because it was presumed to be made from תמד. Today it must be tithed, because it is presumed to be made from wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said: In Judea, in the early days, someone who bought vinegar from an עם הארץ did not need to tithe it, because the presumption was that it came only from תמד. But now, someone who buys vinegar from an עם הארץ must tithe it, because the presumption is that it comes only from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the same then-and-now change in wine, this time with a practical halachic result for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since old Judean wine would not sour by itself, vinegar was usually made from תמד, which is water soaked through leftover grape skins and seeds. The ברייתא seems to assume that תמד needs no tithing, so the vinegar needed none. Step 9 challenges that assumption, and steps 10-11 explain what רבי יהודה really meant. Today wine sours easily, so vinegar is presumed to be real wine and must be tithed.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person, suspected of not tithing properly
A drink made by soaking leftover grape skins and seeds in water
A presumption about how things usually are

steps.confusionAlert: תמד is not wine. It is mostly water that picked up flavor from grape leftovers. That is why it can be treated differently from wine for מעשר.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In Judea, in the early days,
one who buys vinegar from an am ha'aretz
does not need to tithe it,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁחֲזָקָה אֵינוֹ בָּא אֶלָּא מִן הַתֶּמֶד.
phrases.english: because the presumption is that it comes only from temed.
But now, one who buys vinegar from an am ha'aretz
must tithe it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחֶזְקָתוֹ אֵינוֹ בָּא אֶלָּא מִן הַיַּיִן.
phrases.english: because its presumption is that it comes only from wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בִּיהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא showing the same change in wine strength, now with a halachic result for tithing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vinegar bought from an עם הארץ was once exempt from tithing because it was presumed to be תמד. Today it must be tithed because it is presumed to be from wine.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה elsewhere obligates תמד in tithing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. A משנה shows that רבי יהודה obligates תמד in tithing even when no extra liquid came out of the grapes. So how could he say vinegar from תמד needs no tithing?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold that תמד is not subject to tithing? But we learned in a משנה: One who makes תמד and puts in a measured amount of water, and then finds only the same amount of liquid, is exempt. And רבי יהודה obligates him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a contradiction. רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא seems to clash with his own opinion in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the grape leftovers added no volume, only taste, so the חכמים exempt it. רבי יהודה obligates tithing even then. If he obligates even that kind of תמד, he should not have exempted vinegar presumed to come from תמד.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: תֶּמֶד לָאו בַּר עַשּׂוֹרֵי הוּא?
phrases.english: Does Rabbi Yehuda hold that temed is not subject to tithing?
But we learned:
One who makes temed and put in a measured amount of water,
and found only the amount he measured, is exempt,
phrases.notes: No grape juice added volume, only flavor.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda obligates him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: תֶּמֶד לָאו בַּר עַשּׂוֹרֵי הוּא? וְהָא (תְּנַן)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind רבי יהודה's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא that vinegar presumed to come from תמד needs no tithing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a משנה, רבי יהודה obligates tithing even on תמד that added no volume. So he holds that תמד is subject to tithing, which contradicts his exemption in the ברייתא.

steps.title: עמי הארץ are not suspected about תמד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does hold that תמד needs tithing. The ברייתא only means that an עם הארץ is trusted to have tithed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יהודה means: עמי הארץ were never suspected of skipping the tithe on תמד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. Both sources agree that תמד needs tithing. The ברייתא only says we trust the עם הארץ to have tithed it already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about the basic law: תמד must be tithed. The ברייתא is about trust: vinegar bought from an עם הארץ needs no tithing because we assume he already tithed the cheap תמד. So the two sources discuss different questions and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a reinterpretation)
Unlearned people who are not trusted to tithe carefully
A weak drink made by soaking grape leftovers in water

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean that תמד is free from tithing. It means the עם הארץ is assumed to have already tithed it.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ עַל הַתֶּמֶד.
phrases.english: Amei ha'aretz were not suspected regarding temed.
phrases.notes: תמד is cheap, so they did not mind tithing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the ברייתא is about trust, not about the basic obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that תמד needs no tithing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: תמד needs tithing, but עמי הארץ are trusted to have tithed it.

steps.title: Two kinds of תמד: from dregs or from pits
steps.stepSummary: Even if עמי הארץ are suspected, there is no contradiction. The משנה is about תמד made from dregs, and the ברייתא is about תמד made from grape pits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, say that they were suspected. Still, this is no problem: this source is about תמד made from dregs, and that source is about תמד made from pits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. It splits the two sources into two different kinds of תמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dregs still hold some real wine, so their תמד must be tithed, which is the משנה. Pits hold no wine, so their תמד is free, which is the ברייתא. This answer works even if we do not trust the עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: If you wish, say: they were suspected,
and it is not difficult:
This one (the mishna) is about dregs,
phrases.notes: Dregs contain some wine, so tithing is required.

phrases.english: that one (the baraita) is about grape pits.
phrases.notes: Pits have no wine, so tithing is not required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the same קשיא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same kind of תמד.
steps.terutzMaskana: תמד from dregs must be tithed, and תמד from pits is free.
steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction about רבי יהודה has two answers: (1) עמי הארץ are trusted with תמד; (2) dregs-תמד needs tithing, but pits-תמד does not.

steps.title: What is זיתום המצרי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of חמץ items and asks what זיתום המצרי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'Egyptian זיתום' and so on. What is Egyptian זיתום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the vinegar topic. It quotes the next item in the משנה and asks for a definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple request for information. It is not an attack. Before we know why זיתום counts as חמץ, we need to know what it is made of.

keyTerms.meaning: Egyptian זיתום, a kind of beer
Etc. (the quote of the משנה continues)

phrases.english: 'And Egyptian zitom,' etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: What is Egyptian zitom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new item in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ingredients make up זיתום המצרי

steps.title: רב יוסף: barley, safflower and salt
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that זיתום is made of equal thirds: barley, safflower and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: one third barley, one third safflower, and one third salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a teaching from רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Barley is one of the five grains that can become חמץ. That is why זיתום counts as חמץ, even though grain is only one third of the mix.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
one third barley,
one third safflower,
and one third salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Equal parts barley, safflower and salt

steps.title: רב פפא puts wheat in place of barley, with a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the grain in זיתום is wheat, not barley. The גמרא gives the word סיסני to help remember who said which version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא takes out the barley and puts in wheat. Your memory aid is 'סיסני' (twig baskets).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the recipe from רב פפא. It then adds a memory aid so we do not mix up the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions differ only in which grain is used. Either way, the drink is חמץ. The aid סיסני has the 'S' sound, which links רב יוסף (with a ס) to שעורים, barley (with a ש that sounds like ס).
steps.whatToRemember: זיתום המצרי is a grain-based drink made of one third grain, one third safflower and one third salt. רב יוסף says the grain is barley, and רב פפא says it is wheat.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa removes the barley
and inserts wheat,
and your mnemonic is 'sisanei.'
phrases.notes: The 'S' sound links רב יוסף to שעורים (barley).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא מַפֵּיק שְׂעָרֵי וּמְעַיֵּיל חִיטֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב יוסף's recipe
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In זיתום המצרי, the grain is wheat instead of barley.

steps.title: How זיתום המצרי Is Prepared and Its Effects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes how זיתום is made and drunk, how it affects digestion, and who should not drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They soak the ingredients, roast them, grind them, and drink the mixture from פסח until שבועות. It loosens someone who is constipated and firms up someone whose bowels are loose. But for a sick person or a pregnant woman it is dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining זיתום. Steps 13-14 gave its ingredients, and now it tells us how people prepare it and use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ingredients include grain (barley according to רב יוסף, wheat according to רב פפא), and the grain is soaked in water. That is why זיתום counts as a mixture containing חמץ. The health details are background information about how people actually used this drink.

phrases.english: They soak them and roast them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the three ingredients of זיתום.

phrases.english: and grind them and drink them
from Passover until Shavuot.
phrases.notes: This is the season when people drank it.

phrases.english: For one who is constipated, it loosens him,
and for one who is loose, it firms him up.
For a sick person or a pregnant woman, it is dangerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the definition of זיתום by describing how it is prepared and used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זיתום is soaked, roasted, ground, and drunk between פסח and שבועות. It regulates digestion but is dangerous for the sick and for pregnant women.

steps.title: Defining Dyers' Broth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes זומן של צבעים from the משנה and explains that it is bran water used in dyeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'dyers' broth'. Here in בבל they explained: it is bran water that dyers use when they dye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next item on the משנה's list and defines it. It quotes the משנה's words and then gives the explanation used in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bran is the outer husk of grain, so water soaked with bran contains grain material that can become חמץ. This is why it appears on the משנה's list.

phrases.english: [The mishna's] 'And dyers' broth,' etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Here (in Babylonia) they explained:
bran water
phrases.notes: Water that bran was soaked in.

phrases.english: that they use for dyeing.
phrases.notes: Commentators explain the last word in different ways, for example as the name of a dye or as leather being dyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from זיתום to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זומן של צבעים is bran water used in dyeing.

steps.title: Defining Cooks' Dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that עמילן של טבחים is a loaf made from unripe grain, placed on a pot to soak up the scum.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'cooks' dough'. This is bread made from grain that had not yet reached one-third of its ripeness. The cook places it on the mouth of a pot, and it absorbs the scum.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the next item on the משנה's list by describing what it is made from and how cooks used it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This bread was not made for eating. It was a kitchen tool for cleaning the pot. It still contains grain, so it appears on the list of חמץ items.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'grain that did not reach one-third' with flour that is one-third of a mixture. 'שליש' here measures how ripe the grain was when it was harvested.

phrases.english: [The mishna's] 'And cooks' dough,' etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: It is bread made from grain that did not reach one-third ripeness,
which one places on the mouth of a pot
and it absorbs the scum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of definitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמילן של טבחים is a loaf of under-ripe grain used to absorb scum from a pot.

steps.title: Defining Scribes' Paste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that קולן של סופרים is, according to the explanation used in בבל, shoemakers' flour paste.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'scribes' paste'. Here in בבל they explained: it is shoemakers' paste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the next item on the משנה's list, קולן של סופרים, using the explanation from בבל. The next steps bring a different explanation and debate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a glue made from flour, so it contains grain that can become חמץ. In בבל they identified it with the paste that shoemakers used.
steps.whatToRemember: Every item discussed (זיתום, זומן, עמילן, קולן) is a mixture that contains grain. That is why each one is treated as a mixture containing חמץ.

phrases.english: [The mishna's] 'And scribes' paste,' etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Here (in Babylonia) they explained it:
shoemakers' paste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the series of definitions for the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קולן של סופרים is shoemakers' flour paste.

steps.title: רב שימי: It is the wealthy girls' hair-removal paste
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי מחוזנאה explains קולן של סופרים as the hair-removal paste of wealthy girls, which they left over for poor girls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי from חוזנאה said: This is the hair-removal paste of wealthy girls, which they leave over for the daughters of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different explanation of קולן של סופרים, the item in the משנה we just discussed. רב שימי says it is a beauty paste, not a glue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The paste contained flour, so it could contain חמץ. According to this view, the name comes from wealthy girls giving their leftover paste to poor girls, whose fathers were often poor schoolteachers (סופרים). So 'סופרים' here does not refer to a trade at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Their cosmetic paste (here, a hair-removal paste)

phrases.english: Rav Shimi from Chozna'a said:
This is the cosmetic (hair-removal) paste of wealthy girls,
phrases.notes: A paste made with flour, so it can involve חמץ.

phrases.english: which they leave over for the daughters of the poor.
phrases.notes: The poor girls' fathers were schoolteachers (סופרים), which explains the name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of קולן של סופרים than the shoemakers' paste in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קולן של סופרים is the hair-removal paste of wealthy girls, left over for poor girls.

steps.title: Challenge: The משנה's list includes tradesmen's items
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that the משנה lists four common household items and three tradesmen's items. A beauty paste is not a trade item, so רב שימי's explanation does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי חייא taught: four kinds of items used by ordinary people of the country, and three kinds of tradesmen's items. If you say it is the paste of wealthy girls, what trade is involved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב שימי's explanation using a teaching of רבי חייא about how the משנה's list is organized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא divides the משנה's list into two groups. The common items are כותח, beer, vinegar, and זיתום. The trade items are the dyers' bran water, קולן של סופרים, and the cooks' loaf. If קולן של סופרים were a girl's beauty paste, it would not belong in the tradesmen's group.

keyTerms.meaning: Items used by ordinary people of the country
Items used in a trade or craft

phrases.english: Is that so? But Rabbi Chiya taught:
four kinds of items of ordinary people of the country,
phrases.notes: כותח, beer, vinegar, and זיתום.

phrases.english: and three kinds of tradesmen's items.
phrases.notes: Dyers' bran water, קולן של סופרים, and the cooks' loaf.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ טִיפּוּלָן שֶׁל בְּנוֹת עֲשִׁירִים,
phrases.english: And if you say it is the cosmetic paste of wealthy girls,
what tradesmen's item is there in that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב שימי's explanation in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי's explanation that קולן של סופרים is a beauty paste
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא says the item belongs to the tradesmen's group. A girls' cosmetic is not a trade item, so it cannot be what the משנה means.

steps.title: Counter-question: Then why is it named after scribes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if it is shoemakers' paste, the משנה should have called it shoemakers' paste, not scribes' paste.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is it? Shoemakers' flour paste? Then why is it called 'scribes' paste'? It should have been called 'leatherworkers' paste'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the other explanation, that it is shoemakers' paste. This sets up רב אושעיא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Explaining it as shoemakers' paste solves the 'trade item' problem. But it creates a naming problem: why would the משנה name it after סופרים and not after leatherworkers? This counter-question explains why רב שימי looked for a different explanation.

phrases.english: Rather, what is it? Shoemakers' flour paste?

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ הַאי קוֹלָן שֶׁל סוֹפְרִים?
phrases.english: Why does it call this 'scribes' paste'?
It should have said 'leatherworkers' paste'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 with a counter-challenge to the shoemakers' explanation from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that קולן של סופרים is shoemakers' paste
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were shoemakers' paste, the name would mention shoemakers, not scribes.

steps.title: רב אושעיא: Shoemakers' paste that scribes also use
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says it really is shoemakers' paste. It is called scribes' paste because scribes also use it to glue their papers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: Really, it is shoemakers' flour paste. Why is it called scribes' paste? Because scribes also glue their papers with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא answers the naming problem and keeps the shoemakers' paste explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scribes also used the paste to attach their papers, so it could be called after them. This keeps it a trade item, which fits רבי חייא's teaching. It also explains the name סופרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeps the original position)

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion is that קולן של סופרים is a flour-based glue used by craftsmen, including scribes. That is why it counts as a tradesmen's item in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
Really, it is shoemakers' flour paste,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ קוֹלָן שֶׁל סוֹפְרִים?
phrases.english: and why is it called scribes' paste?
Because scribes also glue their papers with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: לְעוֹלָם פֵּרוּרָא דְאוּשְׁכָּפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the naming question raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the name reflects a second group that also uses the item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling it 'scribes' paste' suggests it is not shoemakers' paste.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is shoemakers' paste, and it is named for scribes because they use it too.

steps.title: Can jewelry really contain חמץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר in the משנה, 'also women's jewelry', and asks how jewelry could be relevant to חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: also women's jewelry, etc. Could you really think it means women's jewelry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and questions רבי אליעזר's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jewelry is made of gold, silver, or woven materials, which have no grain. So it makes no sense to forbid jewelry because of חמץ. The question shows that the word must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר אַף תַּכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: also women's jewelry, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Could you really think it means women's jewelry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי אליעזר's addition in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal wording תכשיטי נשים in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Jewelry contains no grain, so it cannot be forbidden as חמץ.

steps.title: Read it as women's cosmetics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the phrase as טיפולי נשים, meaning women's cosmetics.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: also women's cosmetics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by changing how we read the phrase. It means cosmetics, not jewelry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cosmetic pastes could contain flour, so they could involve חמץ. Reading the phrase as 'cosmetics' makes רבי אליעזר's addition make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (read the text this way)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture rings or necklaces here. The גמרא makes clear that רבי אליעזר means cosmetic preparations.

phrases.english: Rather, say: also women's cosmetics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means women's cosmetics, which can contain flour.

steps.title: Support from רב יהודה in the name of רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting רב יהודה in the name of רב about Jewish girls, to support the 'cosmetics' reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Jewish girls...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof that women used such cosmetics. The quote continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement will show that Jewish girls used beauty preparations, so 'women's cosmetics' is a real category. The full content comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Jewish girls...
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins supporting the 'cosmetics' reading from step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That טיפולי נשים, women's cosmetics, were a real practice
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב (continues on the next amud)
